# montecarlo_salesforce_crm_credentials (Resource)

Salesforce CRM credentials are the sign-in Monte Carlo stores for Salesforce CRM connections to use: a user with a password and security token, or a connected app's OAuth client. The password, the security token and the consumer secret are never returned.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auth_mode` (String) How Monte Carlo signs in. `password` takes `username`, `password` and `security_token`. `oauth_client_credentials` takes `consumer_key`, `consumer_secret` and `domain`.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `consumer_key` (String) Consumer key of the connected app Monte Carlo signs in as, for `oauth_client_credentials`.
- `consumer_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Consumer secret of the connected app, for `oauth_client_credentials`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `consumer_secret_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `consumer_secret_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `domain` (String) My Domain of your org, such as `acme.my.salesforce.com`, for `oauth_client_credentials`. The `.salesforce.com` suffix is optional.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of `username`, for `password`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `password_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `security_token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Security token of `username`, for `password`. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `security_token_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `security_token_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `username` (String) Salesforce user Monte Carlo signs in as, for `password`.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
